geography: US labor-cost scenarios; public USD vendor anchors
period: Annual undiscounted scenarios; monthly inputs explicitly named. No inflation, tax, discount rate or revenue growth is implicit.
status: Inputs only. All customer savings, rates, prices, hosting, support, CAC, churn and adoption counts are scenario hypotheses unless linked as a source fact. No model results or buyer observations.

units.hours: person-hours, not elapsed wall-clock time; annual staffing capacity assumes 2080 hours only as a convention
units.fraction: 0 to 1; sensitivity endpoints are independently varied, not joint probability bounds
units.monthly: per account per calendar month unless otherwise named
units.annual_accounts: average active paid accounts maintained during a steady-state year; initial-acquisition cash scenario must be reported separately

rate_basis.explanation: USD 100 engineering/hour is a rounded modeling assumption near May 2025 annual developer wages spread across 2080 assumed hours and a broad June 2026 benefits loading. The surveys measure different populations and dates. USD 54 reviewer/hour uses broad full-time private compensation as an anchor, not an observed reviewer wage. Neither includes a measured SignalTree-specific productivity value.

default_analysis_rules: Show capacity value separately from cash savings; cash_release_fraction defaults to zero. Apply capacity realization only to avoided task hours, not to adoption or operations cost.

First-year migration assumes no greenfield build credit. one_time_build_hours_avoided is available only in a separately labeled new-module counterfactual, and never added to hours already saved in recurring maintenance.
For paired v15/v16 analysis use the same account and v15 baseline. v16 adds only v16_increment_over_v15 benefits/costs plus its separately measured performance delta.
Private Studio benefit is incremental over the existing runtime and existing monitoring. Evaluate this separately before combining it with runtime value.

Keep all four recurring work buckets disjoint: v15 maintenance, v16 coordination maintenance, Studio engineering investigation, and operational review. Fix implementation work is excluded from investigation hours.
All source prices are anchors for alternatives, not validated pricing authority. All SignalTree paid prices apply only to future private offers, never the free public runtime.
Risk default is zero. Use the illustrative risk branch only with conspicuous hypothetical labeling and loss excluding already counted labor.
Performance input is left to measured application evidence; recoverable blocking-time value defaults to zero. No memory or browser delay is automatically converted into customer money.
A stable account count needs replacement acquisitions for churn; show replacement CAC and replacement onboarding. Initial acquisition of the entire account base is a separate cash requirement.
Do not count variable support/onboarding or sales acquisition costs again in fixed payroll. Charge founders labor and OSS maintenance even if unpaid.
Supplier profit is operating profit before income tax/financing, only after explicit labor, hosting, support, acquisition and fixed costs. ARR is not profit.

Aggregate net resource benefit removes subscription transfers and includes supplier real resource costs, free-runtime maintenance and customer integration/operations. It must not also count supplier revenue as newly created value.

customer_tiers.scenario_status: unobserved illustrative account, not an empirical industry-size representative

v15_runtime.counterfactual: A competent implementation using an existing free framework/state library, retaining durable backend authority and existing observability.
v15_runtime.benefit_boundary: Local state/entity maintenance only; excludes v16 coordinated-pending plumbing, Studio investigation, review, backend authorization, model quality and agent productivity.

v16_increment_over_v15.counterfactual: v15 plus application code to implement only the additional coordinated pending/local publication behavior needed by this account; no equivalence for unmeasured full semantics is asserted.
v16_increment_over_v15.benefit_boundary: Disjoint coordinated-pending implementation/maintenance hours, beyond the v15 bucket. The small account has zero assumed recurring need and still incurs adoption cost.

private_studio.counterfactual: Existing runtime plus the same tracing, monitoring and durable workflow services; no existing vendor subscription is removed.
private_studio.hosting_cost_treatment: Hypothetical hosted offer includes hosting in subscription; supplier COGS is separate. Customer self-hosting would replace this assumption with measured costs.
private_studio.benefit_boundary: Only marginal investigation and evidence-review work beyond existing tools, separate from building/fixing code and nonlabor losses.
private_studio.readiness: Future private-tool offer. Broader v16 private checks do not establish hosted multi-tenant, production IdP or SLA readiness. v15 has only narrow transaction-delegation checks, not full Studio qualification.

risk_illustrative_sensitivity.status: Pure hypothetical sensitivity, not observed incident prevalence or efficacy. Loss excludes all labor already counted, insurance recovery, transferred payments and unproven fines.

capacity_realization_fraction.unit: fraction of avoided task hours converted to usable capacity

v15_runtime.recurring_build_maintenance_.unit: fraction of disjoint relevant baseline hours

v16_increment_over_v15.recurring_coordin.unit: fraction of disjoint relevant baseline hours

ongoing_operations_multiplier.unit: multiplier applied to each incremental monthly operations-hours input

hosting_anchor_limit: R2 rates only establish that raw storage is one small component. Scenario hosting inputs also need compute, database/indexing, security, backup and operations; none is a measured Studio deployment.

telemetry_sensitivity_inputs.status: Independent illustrative volume grid, not measured production event sizes or a selected architecture. Use real counts and retention before estimating a bill.
